scoreMeaning: Subjective expert judgment of the stated static visual scope, not a precise measurement or audience result. The quieter antenna is a modest gain; remaining material and scale limitations do not justify raising my prior 8.4 or awarding 9. The new signature placement is now included explicitly.
strengths: The oversized cream head, compact torso, unequal paddles, small mittens, attached feet and layered green wings remain endearing. The source diff changes paint plumbing rather than anatomy; shown poses preserve the same innocent construction.

The selected .62 night antenna edge is less insistent than the .85 control in paint.png while retaining connected stems in the shown 96/128/160px full figures. Neither broad glow nor additional texture has been introduced.
Cream remains matte and face-first against the greens. The soft-falloff candidate slightly broadens the light area without a shiny highlight or a palette shift.

Keeping the original whole-character rim is defensible: the reduced-rim comparison weakens outer boundary definition without a convincing improvement in hand/ruff articulation. My earlier reduction hypothesis is not a requirement to reduce it.

Desktop signature scale gives the face and open wing enough space to sit naturally beside the project question. The phone single-theme studio also gives the character a substantially clearer visual presence than the phone signature.

deductions.severity: moderate polish; nonblocking for local study
deductions.confidence: high for observed still detail, not recognition
deductions.basis: At 96px in sizes-refined.png, glasses, mittens and ruff still form a dense central drawing. Grateful retains a small loop cluster in poses.png; intentional contact is legitimate, but individual hand contours remain less immediate than the face and wings. Paint does not solve this staging/scale tradeoff.

deductions.confidence: high for layout; moderate for its expressive impact
deductions.basis: signature-390.png keeps a narrow side-by-side stage, reducing the figure to a small companion while the question occupies the dominant column. Its small right mitten and facial nuance are less available than in signature-1440.png or studio-390-single.png. This limits fine visual acting, not text comprehension.

The soft-falloff difference in paint.png is restrained enough that cream and forewings still read primarily as clean graphic planes. I see a small tonal benefit, not a substantial increase in softly modelled volume or tactile appeal.

improvementCriteria: At intended full-figure sizes, demonstrate clearer meaningful hand contact or negative space while preserving clasped gratitude and the tiny anatomy; do not require blanket hand separation.
Compare a phone signature composition with more usable character width while retaining the visible project cue; adopt only if relevant face/mitten details become clearer without weakening reading.

A future material alternative must show a named soft-volume benefit in matched poses and actual applications without gloss, noisy texture, lost contours or changed anatomy. Retaining current paint remains valid.
confidence: Moderate overall. High on source preservation and shown framing, moderate on subjective softness; no continuous playback or calibrated-display evidence.

implementedAssessment.decision: Retain refined paint for the documented local supported grounds and sizes, with named nonblocking limits. No serious visual regression found.

challengedClaims.assessment: Supported by the exact character.js diff and matching hashes. geometry.json reports zero mismatches over 567 samples; I inspected that result but did not rerun it. Paint/filter exclusions mean it does not establish pixel-identical contours or artistic quality.

challengedClaims.claim: Quieter antenna and softer falloff improve the result
challengedClaims.assessment: Accept a modest local-edge gain and a slight tonal gain. The 16-unit keyline width and underlying paths remain unchanged; only its opacity changes. Broad tactile-equivalence or recognition claims would exceed the PNG evidence.

The documented paper-ground day avatar remains the appropriate universal 32/48/64px option. Fine stems are weak in the 32px night alternative. harness.html loads header PNGs from assets while the avatar/full-figure rows use the current renderer; these header controls cannot certify newly regenerated exports.

skillsReviewed.application: Workflow review requested by Nag; no new prototype, browser session, source edit or motion certification performed.

workflowChanges: Add an instant, one-variant-at-a-time review at actual application size to the existing matched comparison sheets. Contact sheets remain useful for diagnosis; realistic single-variant context decides whether the material difference survives normal viewing.

Keep each experiment on a named axis and record its benefit/cost: local antenna prominence, whole-character boundary definition, matte tonal falloff, or available character width. The current isolated paint catalogue already follows this useful discipline.

Use lead/support/static roles when assessing future visual staging: the noticed cue and character attention carry the meaning; surrounding copy, controls and background need no competing entrance animation. Story order can justify deliberate sequencing.

Report source validity, static appeal, continuous-motion perception and hardware performance separately. For the retained SVG rim, require a measured paint/frame-cost problem before changing filters or adding will-change; PNGs cannot establish speed on a phone.

Carry the mobile-native distinction into application reviews: capability-gated hover and coarse-pointer select text address plausible platform problems, while physical-device input zoom, touch feel and Safari rendering remain unverified. Root owns the announced UI fixes and fresh evidence.
Preserve Nag’s Investigate & share selection as personal-fit direction for subsequent visual reviews; do not turn owner preference into an artistic score increase or evidence of stranger recognition.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Sub-300ms UI motion and no keyboard-triggered animation
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: Apply to interface feedback and frequent navigation, not the intentionally requested multi-second character performance. Keyboard activation of Play must retain access to the same authored performance, with reduced-motion handling.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Only transform/opacity; replace JavaScript motion automatically
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: The native SVG renderer deforms antenna, eye and mouth paths for expressive correctness. A blanket compositor rewrite would change the drawing. Diagnose actual frame cost before optimizing; no device recording was inspected.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Add blur, spring bounce, stagger or press-scale as universal polish
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: These are contextual techniques. They cannot hide contact errors, justify extra glow or replace the current character timing without a named benefit. Existing direct press feedback need not become scale feedback.
Meaningful stills and manually inspected timeline frames already communicate the character. No unsolicited fade or movement is required merely to satisfy a generic UI preference.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Prototype hard rule to delete the exploration surface after selection
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: This repository explicitly requires retained controls, editable variants and review evidence. Preserve those authorized records; the skill’s separate user-choice workflow is not being invoked to rebuild the already implemented study.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Default to flagging or block on every generic style rule
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: AGENTS.md requires evidence-backed judgments and no invented defects. The review keeps actual material/scale concerns and does not manufacture an objection from unrelated UI conventions.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Apply the complete mobile-native baseline globally
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: The signature is a scrolling study, not an installed fullscreen app. Do not suppress ordinary scrolling, text selection, zoom or native feedback without a specific reason. Hardware-only claims remain open.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: All other catalogue skills must run
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: Cataloguing is not task authorization to edit unrelated systems. Swift, Expo, Sonner, dependency selection, animation naming and destructive motion-removal workflows do not fit this static visual review.
